def: The PCIe packet that carries a request (memory, I/O, configuration, message) or a completion between two devices.
A small link-local PCIe packet used for acknowledgements (Ack/Nak), flow-control credit updates and power management; it never leaves the link it was sent on.
An NVMe data pointer entry naming a host memory page (the first may carry an offset); a transfer is described by PRP1, PRP2 and, for longer transfers, PRP lists.
The PCIe extended capability and mechanism for detailed logging and reporting of correctable and uncorrectable errors, including a header log of the offending TLP.
The 64-byte NVMe command structure the host writes into a Submission Queue slot and the controller fetches by DMA.
The 16-byte NVMe structure a controller writes into a Completion Queue to report a command's result: command-specific DW0, SQ head and ID, CID, phase tag and status.
A 16-bit value chosen by the host in CDW0 of an SQE and echoed in the CQE; unique among outstanding commands on one Submission Queue.
The largest TLP data payload a function may send or must accept, programmed in Device Control; it must be consistent along a path. (NVMe's CC.MPS is an unrelated memory page size field.)
The address alignment (64 or 128 bytes) at which a completer may split the completions for a memory read.
PCIe interrupt mechanism in which a function signals an interrupt by writing a programmed data value to a programmed address taken from a per-vector table in one of its BARs.
Bit 16 of CQE DWORD 3; the controller inverts the value it writes on each pass through a Completion Queue, so the host can tell new entries from old ones.
The earliest observation (a row, or the absence of an expected row) that departs from what the specifications and the system's configuration predict; later errors may be its consequences.
The 32-bit CRC the Data Link Layer appends to each TLP on a link; a receiver that finds it wrong discards the TLP and sends a Nak, causing a replay.
A PCIe uncorrectable error recorded by a requester when the completions for a non-posted request do not arrive within its programmed timeout window.
A TLP whose EP bit is set, marking its data as known to be bad; the receiver must not use the data as if it were good and reports the event through error handling.
A flow-control DLLP by which a receiver returns credits to its link partner, carrying cumulative header and data credit values for one traffic type (posted, non-posted, completion).
A known-good capture of an operation on a specific platform, kept as a reference so that new captures can be compared against it to find the first difference.
An instrument that records the traffic on a link (both directions, timestamped) without taking part in the protocol, and decodes it in software into packets, transactions and higher-level operations.
A probe board inserted between a device and its connector (or slot) so that an analyzer can observe the link; it adds length and loss to the electrical channel.
A condition evaluated by an analyzer in real time that marks a point in the capture and determines how much traffic before and after it is kept.
An analyzer setting that discards selected traffic before it is stored; unlike a display filter, the discarded events are absent from the trace file.
A non-posted PCIe request together with the completion(s) that answer it, matched by Requester ID and Tag; the request and its completions travel separately.
The flow-control-unit based encoding and packet framing introduced with PCIe 6.x; TLP headers use a different format from the earlier non-flit layout.
The capture file as stored on disk, often in a vendor-proprietary format; the original evidence from which decodes and exports are derived.
The recorded origin and handling history of a capture or derived file: source, hashes, tools and versions, settings, conversions and redactions.
In PCIe work, either a capture-file extension commonly associated with Teledyne LeCroy PCIe analyzer software, or Broadcom's PEX-series PCIe switch family; establish which is meant.
